evidence: real but needs two messages in two sessions within about a second; the beat is now written at once (test 'RV-001 F5'), which closes the delay but not a true simultaneous race; a machine-wide ledger is not worth it at this scale

claim: the status file carries the session's absolute folder, which docs say it never does

claim: an untracked symlink sends a file from outside the repo (e.g. ~/.ssh/config) to the reviewer

claim: a beat just after midnight credits yesterday's minutes to the new day
evidence: minutesToday summed whole credits; clipped at midnight now (test 'RV-001 F8')

claim: syncNow commits (git add + commit) before checking for another session's rebase, so it can mark conflicted files resolved and move HEAD inside that rebase
evidence: syncNow called commit before the rebase check, which lived only in pull; now rebaseUnderWay is checked before any git command in syncNow and initBrain. The suggested machine-wide lock was not added: with the check and git's index.lock the remaining window is the instant between the check and the add, and $.fs has no exclusive create. claim: open sessions are told only about new note ids, not notes approved or retired by another session
evidence: reload selected !before.has(e.id) only; now approvals arrive like new notes and retirements of notes Claude was using arrive under 'No longer true' (test 'RV-002 F2', fails without the fix)

claim: a merge can retire the user's protected note listed in with, and verdicts are accepted for notes outside the review queue
evidence: merge members were only checked to exist, and protection was computed from the primary note alone; now members must be same-project pending or live notes of reviewable kinds, a guarded or unsettled member makes the merge the user's call, and refs must be in the queue (test 'RV-002 F3', fails without the fix)

claim: a session open across two midnights disappears from /glance and from beat accounting
evidence: readLive read only today's and yesterday's folders while a session writes to its opening day's folder; now every retained day folder is read, the fresher record wins (test 'RV-002 F4', fails without the fix)

claim: reviewing a note with exactly one earlier version crashes: sameText is not imported
evidence: a regression from the RV-001 F2 fix, which replaced the sameText import with isLive; restored, with a one-ancestor test that fails without it

claim: the 'literal' duplicate check lowercases, so /data/config and /Data/config are dropped as duplicates
evidence: literal() lowercased and collapsed spacing; now only line endings and surrounding space are ignored (test 'RV-002 F5 and F6', fails without the fix)

claim: an untracked file over 200 KB is left out of the packet but the fingerprint hashes only a size marker, so edits that keep the size don't make the packet stale
evidence: fingerprint hashed f.text; now it hashes the real bytes of every untracked file, and a packet that would leave a file out is refused unless --allow-incomplete gives a reason, with complete: no in its header (test 'RV-002 F7', fails without the fix)

claim: a credential in a waiting link's query, or in the reviewer's reason or evidence, is written to the brain unredacted
evidence: safeLink rejected only user:password@ and review rows skipped redact; now secret-named query parameters and the fragment are dropped and every link and reviewer string is redacted through one shared module, hooks/redact.js (test 'RV-003 F1', fails without the fix)

claim: a scheduled run can recall every project's notes and handoffs, against 'only its project's notes and never a handoff'
evidence: recall ignored unattended; now a scheduled run's recall is held to the lean brain: this project's decisions, facts and threads plus approved preferences (test 'RV-003 F2', fails without the fix)

claim: non-Latin notes normalise to nothing, so distinct notes are dropped as duplicates; recall can't find them
evidence: sameText kept only [a-z0-9+#]; now Unicode letters and numbers count (Ship on 周二 vs 周五 are two notes), an empty normalisation never matches, and recall splits words in any script (test 'RV-003 F3', fails without the fix)

claim: a session can report its handoff pushed when its own commit lost git's lock to another session; a machine-wide lock is needed
evidence: the false 'pushed' report is real: the commit result was ignored and ok came from the push alone. Fixed by checking that this session's journal file is committed and nothing is unpushed, retrying once, and reporting 'not pushed yet' otherwise (test 'RV-003 F4', fails without the fix). No note is lost without a lock: it stays on disk and goes out on the next sync. Whether to add the machine-wide lock Codex asks for in three rounds is the owner's call (waiting note LOCK-1)

claim: a merge naming a missing note crashes the reviewer, and a merge can retire a note the user already kept
evidence: a regression in the RV-002 F3 fix: find() returned undefined for a missing member, which passed the check, then m.id threw. Now missing members are refused, members must be reviewable, and a note the user decided is guarded (test 'RV-003 F5', fails without the fix)

claim: two sessions' beats at the same moment can still both credit the same gap; a machine-wide ledger is needed
evidence: the window was widened by waiting on the usage lookup before every write; usage is now looked up on the heartbeat and after turns, so a beat is written straight away (test 'RV-003 F6' hangs and fails without the fix). The remaining race needs two messages within milliseconds; the ledger goes with the lock question (LOCK-1)

claim: a tracked binary change leaves the packet marked complete with only 'Binary files differ' in it
evidence: only untracked files were checked; tracked binary changes now make the packet incomplete unless --allow-incomplete gives a reason (test 'RV-003 F7', fails without the fix). The staleness half was already covered: git's diff carries the new blob hash in its index line

claim: a brainRemote configured with credentials is copied verbatim into HANDOFF.md and pushed
evidence: writeHandoffFile concatenated brain.remote; the install line now carries the remote without user or password, redacted (test 'RV-004 F1', fails without the fix). Latent: the current remote has no credentials

claim: a secret query parameter with an unlisted name (?ticket=) still reaches the brain
evidence: safeLink used a parameter-name denylist; the class is the denylist, so the whole query and fragment are now dropped (test 'RV-004 F2', fails without the fix)

claim: an answer that repeats an existing decision word for word leaves the question open
evidence: the duplicate check continued before the superseding status row; a duplicate now still resolves what it names (test 'RV-004 F3 and F4', fails without the fix)

claim: answering another project's waiting item files the answer under the current project
evidence: project was chosen before the resolved note was looked up; a resolving note now inherits that note's project (test 'RV-004 F3 and F4', fails without the fix)

claim: a usage lookup that never answers hangs session start and the end of every turn
evidence: a regression from the RV-003 F6 fix, which awaited refreshUsage in startLive and turn.complete; it now runs on a timer and publishes when it answers (test 'RV-004 F5', fails without the fix)

claim: a new untracked binary leaves the packet marked complete
evidence: only tracked binaries and oversized files counted as left out; untracked binaries now do too (test 'RV-004 F6', fails without the fix)

claim: two machines with the same hostname share one file

claim: a retired machine's old file, or a later note, blocks confirming forever
evidence: stale had no recency test and absent used only the machine's latest date. Now activity is per day within the week, and a stale file blocks only if it wrote in the 7 days before the week or has notes in it (tests RV-007 F5)

claim: constructor, toString and similar project names resolve inherited properties

claim: the RV-005 F1 test never exercised a lost write: session start consumed the drop

claim: no lock: two sessions can both report success while one adjustment is lost

claim: another machine's unreadable file is silently omitted, so a week confirms without its hours

claim: the comparison-to-write gap remains without a lock or compare-and-swap

LOCK-1 (owner, 10-3) is no lock; this is a lock decision for the owner (waiting note M4-Q2)

claim: a peer file with a bad updated_at passes validSheet and lets a week confirm without its hours

claim: a newer-version or malformed local file passes validSheet and is rewritten as v1, dropping its other fields

evidence: True that takeAnswers -> answerNote -> followUpPrompt -> $.prompt.submit carries a dashboard answer's text into a turn. claim: answer wakes have no durable claim, so they can be missed (asker exits before its refresh) or duplicated (asker's live file stale while it runs)
evidence: Both windows exist: followArrived splices arrivals before acting, and followerOf adds self while others may judge a stale self file dead. They need a session to close within ~2 minutes of an answer, or every live file to be stale at once (after sleep). A miss leaves the answer a decision the next session reads; a duplicate turn is told to check first that nothing has done it. A durable cross-session claim is the machine-wide lock the owner deferred (LOCK-1, ze51hlrn)

claim: a slow successful POST is reported as a timeout and retried five minutes later, so the push arrives twice

claim: a session that has not re-read the brain saves a second decision for a dashboard answer another session already took, and each decision starts a turn

claim: a token under 8 characters is never masked, and /phone off reads the config without masking it

evidence: confirmed for hook scripts, agents and commands: guardedFiles held only settings, CLAUDE.md and .mcp.json (new test fails on the RV-017 code). Not fixed: skills and plugin trees (~/.claude/skills is 682 files, 13 MB here; comparing it after every command is out of proportion) and symlink canonicalisation. A peer turn with a shell can do what the session's permission mode allows, as a SendMessage turn already can; the doc says so. Fix: the restore also covers every file in .claude/hooks, agents, commands and rules under the session folder, the repo's main folder and ~/.claude (200 per folder), and the scripts the guarded settings' hooks run (hookTargets); a file a command added there is emptied

claim: project scope is the folder basename, so an unrelated repository with the same folder name can wake the session
evidence: confirmed: env.project = basename(root) and isForSession compared only that. Severity disputed: the sender also needs the recipient's exact title, and every other brain scope already uses the basename. Fix: addressed notes carry repo = the origin remote as host/owner/name (repoIdOf, credentials stripped); when both note and session have one they must match; either side without one falls back to the folder name. Existing notes have no repo and keep the old rule

claim: a failed delivery-row write leaves no durable row; after a reload the note can be delivered again once the claim is stale
evidence: rejected 'nothing writes the missing row with the next write': append pushes the rows into brain.lines before writing, so any later append writes them. Confirmed that with no later append before a reload the row is lost (new test fails on the RV-017 code). Fix: append marks brain.unwritten on failure and flushJournal rewrites the journal on every poll; a crash with a disk that keeps refusing can still re-deliver after 10 minutes, documented, and the note says check first

claim: README says each note is delivered once on any machine, but same-named sessions on two machines can both take an unpinned note
evidence: the plan doc named the residual; the README row overclaimed. No cross-machine lock exists in a git-synced brain. Fix: README says two machines that each run a session of that name could both take one between syncs

claim: a note from a repository with no remote and the same folder name reaches a session in a repository that has one
evidence: isForSession rejected only when both had a repo. Fix: strict equality of repo ('' included), so a remote-bearing session takes notes only from the same remote and a no-remote one only from no-remote notes; plugin test, pure assertions (old rule returned true)

claim: live records carry no repository, so pinning, namesakes and stuck counts can match a namesake of another repository
evidence: liveRecord had no repo. Fix: live records carry repo; pinDevice pins only on a record whose repo matches (a record from older code never pins); namesakes and stuckNotes count by project and repo (an older record by project alone); live-status.md documents the field

claim: flushJournal and append rewrite the whole file from separate snapshots, so an older write landing last drops newer rows
evidence: two concurrent writes each joined brain.lines when called; the race also existed between two appends before this change. Test with a gated journal write fails on the RV-018 code. Fix: writeJournal runs writes one at a time, each writing all lines known when it starts, and tracks writtenLen; flushJournal writes while writtenLen < lines.length

claim: the restore can empty a file another session creates or edits meanwhile, and walks follow symlinks
evidence: restoreFiles overwrote without keeping the replaced bytes; filesUnder ignored isLink. Test fails on the RV-018 code. Fix: every replaced file's bytes go to ~/.claude/coter-kit/quarantine/<turn time>/ first (a file that can't be saved there is left alone); links in guarded folders are skipped

claim: hookTargets guards every absolute argument, so a hook's log or data file is rolled back
evidence: every absolute word was added. Fix: only the command's program, or the script after a known interpreter (leading VAR= and flags skipped); quoted paths with spaces stay unguarded, and quarantine keeps anything replaced; pure test with log and data arguments

claim: after a resume the act prompt names only ids, so a hook that drops the snapshot leaves notes recorded as delivered unseen
evidence: actPrompt carried no bodies. Fix: an idle snapshot only lists the notes briefly (arrivingSection); the kit's own turn carries them in full (wakePrompt), or the user's next prompt does, and they are recorded once that prompt is in; test fails on the RV-018 code

claim: letters-only secrets (secret-named setting, connection-string password, .env values) were treated as placeholders by a digit/letter check, so they would be sent
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: password: "CorrectHorseBatteryStaple" => [] and Password=OnlyLettersPassword => []
fix: only explicit placeholders are let off (${..}, <..>, your-.., ENV_VAR_NAME, a test word as a part); RV-020 F1 test

claim: files between the 1 MiB scan limit and the 2 MiB export limit, and binaries, were exported without being scanned
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: a recognized secret after 1,048,577 bytes, secretsIn finds it, scan returned []; binaries were skipped by scan but copied
fix: one 1 MiB limit; binaries and larger files are left out and named; the exported bytes are the scanned bytes; RV-020 F2 test

claim: two pages building maps before the guard's update reaches them can pass the 12-request cap (14 reproduced)
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: 14 0. Partial: an edge path (two pages constructing maps in the same window), a few cents, and every Google request is already aborted once the cap is reached, so not high
fix: a load past the cap is a guard failure and an over-cap entry in summary.json; a truly atomic in-page reservation isn't possible (Map is constructed synchronously, bindings are async); RV-020 F3 test

claim: DELETE/PUT/PATCH to Google hosts and an unknown POST to Maps were continued instead of blocked as writes
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: DELETE billed:routes continue; POST unclassified-google continue
fix: default-deny by method before host classification; an unknown Maps POST is a write; RV-020 F4 test

claim: relaying the same round again truncated the first saved answer and its meta
evidence: read relay.mjs: deterministic path, writeFileSync default flag; the new RV-020 F5 test reproduces it (first reply replaced) before the fix. Pre-existing in the old relay, in lines this change touched
fix: exclusive create, a second relay of a round saves as RV-NNN-<reviewer>-2; walk.mjs meta also wx; RV-020 F5 test

claim: unquoted secret-named settings (API_KEY=AbcDef…) went undetected, and a test word anywhere in a value (prod-test-UltraSecretValue) excused it
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: all three lines => []; also found my RV-020 key-boundary change had stopped prefixed names (GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, googleMapsApiKey) matching
fix: a shared secret-name list with _ and camelCase prefixes (no hyphen); an unquoted detector for lines that are only name = value; a test word excuses only a value made of nothing but lowercase words starting or ending with it; RV-021 F1 test with 6 caught and 7 quiet lines

claim: legacy Maps JS DirectionsService (and Distance Matrix, Elevation, legacy Places) ran as unclassified and unbudgeted, and the suite pinned that
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: four requests unclassified-google continue, billed 0
fix: legacy Directions and Distance Matrix count as routes, Elevation as billed, legacy Places as places; an unknown Google GET is blocked and listed (default-deny); a completed unclassified request is a guard failure; two pinned tests re-aimed by name; RV-021 F2 test

claim: found while building RV-021, pre-existing: the packet read the diff before the gates ran but fingerprinted after, so a file edited during the gates gave a packet whose diff lacked the edit yet passed the relay's freshness check
evidence: new test with a gate that appends to app.js: old packet.mjs + lib.mjs let the relay accept it (fails), the fix refuses it as stale
fix: fingerprintOf(repo, snapshot): the packet fingerprints the snapshot its diff came from

claim: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (suffixed name), a quoted connection-string password with spaces, and a real value after a placeholder on the same line were not caught
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: all three => []
fix: names take suffixes; quoted connection-string passwords may hold spaces; every match on a line is judged on its own value; plus the class fix: files whose purpose is secrets (.env*, keys, appsettings*.json, web.config, .npmrc, tfvars, service-account JSON) are never exported; RV-022 F1 test through the relay, and the secret-bearing-file test

claim: Places Autocomplete was free and capped at 20 (places-session), though it bills per request unless its session ends in Details
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: 13 continue, billed 0
fix: Autocomplete counts as billed:places; the places-session kind and its cap are gone; the pinned test re-aimed by name

claim: Roads (and other Maps Platform hosts) were treated as ordinary reads, unbudgeted even past the cap
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: kind read, continue past the cap
fix: the other Maps Platform hosts are billed:other; any other googleapis.com host is default-denied (GET listed as unclassified) unless walk.allowGoogleHosts names it (a Maps host there is refused); fonts, storage and ajax are reads; RV-022 F3 tests

claim: an all-caps credential was treated as an ENV_VAR_NAME placeholder, and quoted secret values with spaces were not parsed
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: API_KEY="ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP1234567890" => [] and PASSWORD="Correct Horse Battery Staple" => []
fix: an ENV_VAR_NAME needs underscore segments; quoted values may hold spaces and count unless they read as a sentence (UI copy); RV-023 F1 test

claim: a path in exportFakes excused every hit in that file, so a real key added to a fixture file would be exported
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: one private-key hit, zero withheld
fix: a path excuses only fixture-shaped kinds; keys and token formats need their exact digest ({ path, digests }), printed by the relay; a .env value is never excused; coter-kit's three fake tokens recorded by digest after checking; RV-023 F2 test through the relay

claim: tracking pixels (Facebook /tr, Mixpanel, self-hosted Matomo) went through a walk as ordinary reads
evidence: ran Codex's Validation: all three read => continue
fix: a long built-in analytics and session-recording host list, pixel paths on shared hosts, Matomo/Piwik on any host, and walk.blockHosts; RV-023 F3 test
